banner.engineNotReady: Welcome! To generate CVs and scan job listings, set up an AI engine in <settings>Settings</settings> — download the free local model, or add an OpenRouter API key.

photo.title: Profile Photo
photo.includeByDefault: Include photo on new CVs by default
photo.adjustHelp: Drag the photo (or use the arrow keys) to reposition it, and use the slider, scroll, or + / − to zoom. Your original upload is never changed.
photo.frameLabel: Photo framing — drag or use the arrow keys to reposition

backup.title: Backup & Restore
backup.help: Move to a new computer or keep a safe copy of your work. Export downloads a single .zip containing your profile & photo, settings, job sources & history, and every generated CV. On the new machine, install Job Coach and use Restore to load that file.
backup.confirmRestore: This replaces your profile, settings, job history and generated CVs on this computer with the contents of the backup. Your API key is kept. This cannot be undone.
backup.note: Restoring replaces your profile, job history and generated CVs with the backup's contents — it does not merge. Your OpenRouter API key is never included in the export and is left untouched on restore.

language.title: Language
language.help: The language of the app's interface. English is the original; other languages are translated by your AI engine.
language.label: App language
language.otherHelp: Type a language name (or its 2-letter code). It will be translated on-device by your AI engine — results may contain rough edges.
language.needEngineFirst: Set up an AI engine above before adding a new language.
language.badCode: We don't recognise that language. Try its English name, or a 2-letter code like sv, ja or ar.

prompts.title: Advanced — AI prompts
prompts.help: These are the exact instructions sent to the AI. The defaults work well — only edit them if you want to change how CVs are written or how job listings are filtered. You can always reset to the default.
prompts.langPlaceholderError: The prompt must contain the {lang_name} placeholder — it tells the AI which language to write in.
prompts.cvHelp: Sent when tailoring a CV. Your profile and the job listing are added automatically below it. {lang_name} is replaced with the output language — it must stay in the prompt.
prompts.extractHelp: Picks which of a page's links are real job openings. The list of links found on the page is added automatically below it.
prompts.filterHelp: Judges each new opening by reading its full posting: decides whether it matches you and pulls out a short digest (employer, location, salary, deadline, requirements). The relevant parts of your profile are added automatically below it.
prompts.letterHelp: Sent when building a cover-letter guide. Your profile and the job listing are added automatically below it. This produces a writing skeleton (3–5 sections with the profile facts to cite, plus writing tips) — never finished letter text. {lang_name} is replaced with the output language — it must stay in the prompt.

preferences.title: Job Preferences
preferences.help: Answer what you can — the Job Coach reads every new job posting against these. Nothing here ever appears on your CV; it is sent to your AI engine each time it reads a posting.

q.roles: Which job titles should we watch for?
q.rolesSub: Add every title you'd actually apply to, including variants and translations. This is the first thing the scanner checks against a listing.
q.rolesPlaceholder: e.g. Data Scientist — press Enter to add
q.where: Where — and how — do you want to work?
q.whereSub: Postings outside these places, languages or working styles get filtered out.
q.locations: Cities or regions you could commute to
q.locationsPlaceholder: e.g. Ghent — press Enter to add
q.great: What makes a job a great match?
q.greatSub: The work, the industry, the mission — whatever would make you genuinely want to apply. Full sentences are fine; the AI reads this like a colleague would.
q.greatPlaceholder: e.g. Research-driven work where I get to build data products end to end, ideally with social impact
q.dealbreakersSub: Even when the title fits. Postings that hit any of these are dropped.
q.dealbreakersPlaceholder: e.g. Purely administrative work, cold acquisition, weekend shifts
q.practicalSub: Salary expectations, contract type, hours, start date, travel — the small print worth catching before you read a posting yourself.
q.practicalPlaceholder: e.g. Full-time from September, at least €3,500/month, max one day of travel a week
q.languagesEmpty: No languages on your profile yet — add the ones you can work in so postings in other languages get filtered out.

preferences.suggestLabel: Common dealbreakers — tap one to add it
preferences.doneSubReady: That's enough to start scanning. Next, tell Job Coach where to look — add a careers page to watch.
preferences.doneSubNoRoles: Add at least one job title in the first question — it's what every listing gets checked against first, so scanning without it finds little.

openrouter.title: OpenRouter
openrouter.desc: Best quality — needs an API key, pay a few cents per use.

qwen3-4b-instruct.name: Qwen3 4B
qwen3-4b-instruct.desc: The recommended default — runs comfortably on a normal laptop, including 8 GB machines without a dedicated graphics card. Multilingual.

gemma-3-4b-it.name: Gemma 3 4B
gemma-3-4b-it.desc: Same size and speed as the default, from a different model family. Try it if you prefer its writing.

qwen3-8b.name: Qwen3 8B
qwen3-8b.desc: Better writing, but roughly twice the memory and about half the speed. Worth it on 16 GB or more; slow on an older laptop.

letters.title: Cover Letter
letters.emptyBody: Paste a job posting URL above to get a tailored plan for writing your letter.

explainer.headline: This tool won't write your letter — that's the point.
explainer.body: A cover letter only works if it’s in your own words; recruiters increasingly discard AI-written ones. Instead, you get a tailored plan: what to say, in what order, and which parts of your profile to use as evidence. The writing stays yours.
